faq: How do you decide the stages?

We ask how a typical deal goes, who is involved and what proof shows it moved forward. Stages describe what the customer did, not what your team hopes. We share a draft first and adjust before we build.
Will my current deals be lost?
No. Open deals stay where they are and we map each old stage to a new one. On Standard and Premium we move them for you and send a before and after list so you can check.
Can the pipeline differ by product?
Yes. If you sell a service and a product with different cycles, we can build separate pipelines. Basic has one pipeline, Standard has two and Premium covers up to four.
Stage design focuses on the structure and the rules. Moving tasks and reminders that run on their own belong to Sales Automations, which you can order separately once the stages are agreed.

desc:
Sales pipeline stages design maps how a deal really moves in your business, then builds those stages in your CRM. Ecom Swift LLC gives each stage a definition, an entry rule and a next step, so everyone describes a deal the same way.

## What are sales pipeline stages?

Sales pipeline stages are the steps a deal passes through from first enquiry to won or lost. Each stage answers one question: where is this customer in the buying process right now? A good pipeline lets anyone on the team look at a deal and know what should happen next.

The names matter less than the meaning. "Qualified" is useful only if everyone agrees what qualifies a lead.

## Why too many stages, or vague ones, hurt you

Many pipelines grow by accident. Someone adds a stage after a lost deal, someone else renames one, and soon the board has eleven columns that nobody uses the same way. A deal marked "negotiation" for one rep is still waiting for a first reply for another.

When stages are unclear, every number built on them is unreliable. Forecasts mix serious opportunities with polite maybes. Managers cannot tell where deals stall. New hires guess, and the CRM turns into a place where deals go to be forgotten.

## How clear stages improve forecasting and focus

Clear stages turn a list of names into a picture of your sales cycle. You can see how much value sits at each step, how long deals stay there and where they tend to drop out. That tells you whether the problem is too few leads, weak qualification or slow proposals.

Stages also guide behavior. When each one has an entry rule and a next step, the owner knows what to do without asking. A lost reason list adds the other half of the story: not just that you lost, but why, whether that was price, timing, a competitor or silence.

## What a well-designed pipeline includes

- A small number of stages, each describing a real step the customer takes.
- A plain definition for every stage that anyone can read in one breath.
- An entry rule saying what must be true before a deal moves in.
- A next step for the owner at each stage.
- Won and lost stages, kept separate from the working stages.
- A lost reason list that is short enough to use consistently.
- Win chance values per stage, where you want a weighted forecast.
- Separate pipelines where the sales process differs, such as new customers and renewals.
- A one page guide your team can keep open while they work.

## How we work

We start by asking you to describe a recent won deal and a recent lost one, step by step. From those stories we draw the path a typical customer takes and remove anything that is only an internal habit. We then propose stage names, definitions and rules for your approval.

Once you agree, we build the pipeline in your CRM and move your existing open deals to the new stages, so nothing disappears. We check the rules on sample deals to confirm they behave properly. The Basic package covers a single pipeline. Standard adds a second pipeline, entry rules and lost reasons. Premium adds more pipelines, win chances, a forecast view and a short period of adjustments once your team starts using it. We do the design work here, while automations are a separate service.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Name stages after what the customer has done, not what your team feels.
- Keep every stage definition short enough to remember.
- Make "lost" require a reason.
- Review the pipeline after a few weeks of real use.
- Give one person responsibility for keeping the stages tidy.

**Avoid:**
- Adding a stage every time a deal behaves oddly.
- Using stages as a to-do list for internal tasks.
- Copying a template from a different industry without testing it on your own deals.
- Letting deals sit in a stage with no next step.
- Sharing one pipeline between very different offers.

## Who this service is for

It suits a team whose pipeline has grown messy and whose forecasts nobody trusts. It suits a business starting its first CRM that wants to avoid inheriting a default pipeline built for someone else. It also suits an owner who sells two kinds of work, for example projects and subscriptions, and needs each one tracked on its own path.

## What we need from you

Share a few recent deals, won and lost, and describe how they progressed. Tell us who sells, what a typical customer asks for and where deals usually stall. We need access to your CRM as an admin or similar user, so we can build the stages in your account. We never ask for passwords. If you already have a pipeline, we also need to know which deals are currently open, so we can place them correctly in the new structure.
